passingJudgment.rationale: The behavior is supported by the cited proposal statements, belongs to the declared capability, and adds only testable detail.

proposalStatements.rationale: The requirements mandate complete paginated REST and GraphQL conversation reads and retain every fetched provider object in the canonical snapshot.

The requirements define versioned deterministic normalization, a canonical digest, preserved provider identities, complete canonical-history retention, and unknown thread state when GraphQL is unavailable.
The requirements provide deterministic reviewer-scoped resources, the complete coordinator conversation, filtering boundaries, and explicit treatment of provider text as untrusted data.
The requirements assign stable identities to new findings, establish ownership from verified provider authorship, and require unique conservative evidence for legacy matching.
Prior targets receive fixed, unfixed, obsolete, or ambiguous classifications with validated actions, but no requirement defines the declared new classification for current findings.
The requirements retain classifications before mutation, route settled owned findings to replies or general comments, and prohibit mutations for ambiguous findings.
The requirements re-fetch and compare both head and complete conversation immediately before mutation, retain stale results, and stop posting on change.
The requirements verify and retain created provider identities and URLs, suppress identical repeated actions, and prohibit changing review-thread resolution.

judgment.rationale: Snapshots, identity, matching, lifecycle, four settled or uncertain prior-finding states, and deterministic planning are specified, but the declared fifth state new is absent from the classification contract.
Stable finding identity, prior/current classification, and identical-rerun suppression support the specified initial and recheck lifecycle.
The requirement directly specifies complete normalized history, deterministic ordering and digesting, preserved provider fields, nullable state, and untrusted text.
It implements stable identities and binds owned targets to verified provider objects retained after creation.
It requires verified App authorship, unique evidence-based matching, and an ambiguous no-mutation outcome when matching is not unique.
It defines evidence-based fixed, unfixed, obsolete, and ambiguous outcomes for owned prior targets and prevents unrelated recheck mutations.
It guards exact-head and conversation freshness and derives repeatable action identity from stable inputs.
All declared provider reads, identity verification, reply routing, and created-object read-back behavior are specified.
It mandates full independent pagination of required REST and GraphQL connections and records unknown resolution when GraphQL cannot provide complete state.
Verified provider author identity supplies the ownership boundary needed for stable targets and owned mutation routing.
It maps owned inline findings to top-level replies and non-thread findings to general status comments, with fail-closed parent selection.
It reads back reviews, enumerates nested inline comments, verifies replies and general comments, and retains their provider identities and URLs.
The requirements specify stable markers, retained pre-mutation plans, constrained status actions, freshness guards, idempotency, and unchanged thread resolution.
Versioned run and finding markers implement stable identity and duplicate detection while excluding untrusted or sensitive marker inputs.
It retains validated classifications and plans before any provider write and makes dry-run execution mutation-free.
It routes settled statuses to existing conversations, suppresses ambiguous mutations, and prohibits new reviews, history edits, and resolution changes.
It checks head and complete conversation before every action, handles verified same-plan writes, and suppresses stable identities already present.
The requirements preserve the registered pipeline, constrain reviewer and coordinator targets, provide complete coordination context, and validate attributed results.
It gives reviewers scoped prior targets through the existing pipeline and rejects identities outside those assignments.
It gives the coordinator complete history and targets, requires exactly one allowed result per applicable target, and excludes provider events from classification output.
It explicitly separates host-authored assignments and schemas from provider text and prevents that text from expanding authority or outputs.
The requirements define isolated host-owned symbolic recheck resources, audit metadata, deterministic bounds, and fail-closed handling of incomplete targets.
It provides reviewer and coordinator history resources outside the checkout and preserves registry isolation and auditable assignment.
Deterministic bounds and atomic target evidence make filtered reviewer views repeatable without partially supplying required identity.
The requirements apply existing path exclusions only to scoped reviewer views while preserving the complete canonical conversation for coordination and safety checks.
It defines deterministic use of existing path classifications for reviewer history without inventing classifications for unbound objects.
It keeps omitted objects in the canonical snapshot for coordination, freshness, idempotency, validation, safety, and audit.

findings.message: The proposal declares a five-state classification including new, but the classification requirement enumerates only fixed, unfixed, obsolete, and ambiguous and explicitly omits newly discovered defects; no requirement defines or emits the new state.
